passage.quote:
TorchLean constructs the backward computation automatically. Checked theorems
connect it to the mathematical VJP under explicit assumptions. Each use identifies
the supported operations and the conditions needed by their derivative rules.

summary: Construct backward computations using actual TorchLean graphs and proved local derivatives.
Prove exact evaluation success and mathematical weighted-output derivatives separately from floating-point and PTX guarantees.
Use PTX and pinned TorchLean definitions in one checked package while keeping exact tensor embeddings separate from kernel correspondence.
remaining: The joint package proves actual graph and tape success, forward polynomial correspondence and mathematical VJP, including an explicit scalar generated-backward result for arbitrary inputs and output seed. Broader graph lowering, backward numerical bounds and independently authored PTX backward correspondence remain open.

from.quote:
The first example computes a pointwise affine transformation followed by squaring:
each output coordinate is `(input * weight + bias)^2` at that coordinate.
Its weight and bias values are differentiable inputs rather than fixed graph
data. The input shape and the output-weight shape are explicit. It uses actual
upstream graph constructors and derivative proofs, so that an independently
recreated toy language cannot satisfy this example.

For an arbitrary tensor of output weights, the bridge establishes both that the
chosen exact backward computation succeeds and that its returned input and
parameter sensitivities are the mathematical vector-Jacobian product. A theorem
that assumes successful evaluation supplies correctness conditional on success;
a separate proof must establish that success under the stated input conditions.
The lower-level exact tape, which stores forward values and local backward rules,
and the checked application interface can have different success conditions.

passage.quote:
theorem checked_success (s : Shape) (inputs : TensorPack ℝ [s, s, s])
    (seed : Tensor ℝ s) :
    let g := (affineSquare s).toTypedGraph (output s)
    g.vjpChecked inputs () seed = .ok (g.vjpWithSeed inputs seed, g.forward inputs) := by
  apply Runtime.Autograd.Torch.TypedGraphWithData.vjpChecked_eq
  rfl

passage.quote:
theorem checked_success_vjp (s : Shape) (inputs : TensorPack ℝ [s, s, s])
    (seed : Tensor ℝ s) :
    let g := (affineSquare s).toTypedGraph (output s)
    flattenCtx (g.vjpWithSeed inputs seed) =
      (fderiv ℝ (fun x => tensorToVec (g.forward (unflattenCtx x)))
        (flattenCtx inputs)).adjoint (tensorToVec seed) := by
  exact checked_vjp s inputs seed _ (checked_success s inputs seed)

from.quote:
For an arbitrary tensor of output weights, the bridge establishes both that the
chosen exact backward computation succeeds and that its returned input and
parameter sensitivities are the mathematical vector-Jacobian product. A theorem
that assumes successful evaluation supplies correctness conditional on success;

The lower-level exact tape, which stores forward values and local backward rules,

passage.quote:
theorem exact_tape_success_vjp (s : Shape) (inputs : TensorPack ℝ [s, s, s])
    (seed : Tensor ℝ s) :
    let g := (affineSquare s).g.toAlgebra
    let gradients := Algebra.Graph.backpropAllCtx g inputs () (TensorPack.single (output s) seed)
    Runtime.Autograd.Tape.backwardDenseAll
        (Algebra.Graph.lowerGraphToTape g inputs ()).1 (output s).i.1
        (Spec.SomeTensor.ofTensor seed) =
      .ok (TensorPack.toShapeErasedArray gradients)
    ∧ flattenCtx (Algebra.TensorPack.takeLeft gradients) =
      (fderiv ℝ (Graph.evalVec (g.toReal ())) (flattenCtx inputs)).adjoint
        (flattenCtx (TensorPack.single (output s) seed)) := by
  apply Algebra.Graph.backwardDenseAll_lowerGraphToTape_adjoint_fderiv_at
  rw [Algebra.Graph.toAlgebra_toReal]
  exact DGraph.graphFDerivCorrectAtOfCorrect (affineSquare s).hg (flattenCtx inputs)

passage.quote:
theorem forward_polynomial (s : Shape) (x w b : Tensor ℝ s) (i : Fin (Spec.Shape.size s)) :
    tensorToVec (((affineSquare s).toTypedGraph (output s)).forward
      (.cons x (.cons w (.cons b .nil)))) i =
    (tensorToVec x i * tensorToVec w i + tensorToVec b i) ^ 2 := by
  simp [Runtime.Autograd.Torch.TypedGraph.forward,
    Runtime.Autograd.Torch.TypedGraphWithData.forward, DGraph.toTypedGraph,
    affineSquare, DGraph.snoc, DGraph.nil, Graph.toAlgebra, Algebra.Graph.toData,
    Algebra.GraphData.eval, Node.toAlgebra, TapeNodes.square, TapeNodes.add,
    TapeNodes.mul, Node.ofFn, output, CtxVec.get_flattenCtx, getIdx, TensorPack.snoc,
    Tensor.castShape, vecOfFun, pow_two,
    get_3_0, get_3_1, get_4_2, get_4_3, get_5_4, get_6_5]

from.quote:
The PTX foundation and integration package use a compatible pinned Lean version.
The integration imports the actual PTX package together with the pinned upstream
TorchLean and mathlib packages. A small shared theorem connects the unsigned
value of the modeled PTX minimum operation to a real scalar tensor; this checks
that definitions and proofs from both libraries can be used together. It does
not identify a PTX kernel with a TorchLean network. The generated-backward proofs
retain their separate exact-real meaning and explicit parameter boundary.

passage.quote:
theorem unsigned_min_scalar_embedding (a b : Ptx.Word) :
    Tensor.item (Tensor.scalar ((Ptx.Scalar.BinOp.eval .minU a b).toNat : ℝ)) =
      (Nat.min a.toNat b.toNat : ℝ) := by
  rw [Tensor.item_scalar, Ptx.Scalar.IntegerMinMax.min_toNat]
